items.title: #1 dedup ratio on the real worktree corpus
items.detail: Full run on 45 slots, 843,889 files, 273.43 GiB raw, 0 errors. Raw 1.00x, per-file zstd 3.60x, whole-file dedup 3.12x, CDC only 5.08x, CDC + zstd 14.04x. A median extra lumen slot costs 0.47 GiB compressed (4.9% of raw). Caveat: 97.5% of raw is cargo target/ and 91.7% is one repo, so 14x is a Rust build-output result. Write-up: docs/spikes/1-dedup-corpus.md. Gate met.

items.title: #2 mmap and file locking over the macOS NFS loopback
items.detail: Viable without sudo (-o locallocks). 24/24 checks. Tuned server: clean builds 0.9x-1.2x native, git status 1.3x-1.4x, warm and incremental builds 2.5x-3.5x (misses 1.5x, see #18). Old server was 3-5x clean and 9-55x warm because of nfsserve bugs (LINK, tracker lock, readdir cookie), fixed in the vendored copy (#19). One 60-dep crate, passthrough server, n=3-5. Write-up: docs/spikes/2-nfs-loopback.md.

items.title: #3 build and git status overhead versus native
items.detail: macOS NFS: clean builds 0.9x-1.2x, warm 2.5x-3.5x. Linux FUSE passthrough in an OrbStack VM (btrfs native): clean 1.03x-1.14x, edit rebuild 1.16x-1.19x, no-op 1.07x-1.48x, seeded first build 1.1x, all within 1.5x. Bulk metadata (git status, find, rm, cp) 2x-3x. Gap looks macOS-NFS-specific (#18). Passthrough only, no ext4 numbers, 7.8k-file tree. docs/spikes/2-nfs-loopback.md and 3-linux-fuse.md

items.title: #4 .git inside the filesystem
items.detail: Reads fine with .git on the mount (status 1.3x, log 1.1x). Writes: add -A 3.9x, commit 3.9x; native .git overlay gives 1.1x and 1.7x. Checkout 9-11x, worktree add 11x, cold status 6.6x in both layouts (working-tree file ops). Found and fixed a write race on read-only-mode files; one unexplained corrupt idx (#21). Large-repo n=3-5, load 15-62. docs/spikes/4-git-inside-the-filesystem.md

items.title: #5 treehouse process detection on the mount
items.detail: cwd-only detection works on the mount for every detectable case. Gap: a process holding an open fd or flock after chdir out is not detected, and on the mount the reset leaves a .nfs silly-rename file and a dirty slot while return exits 0 (#20). lsof and cwd lookup fine. Real pools untouched. docs/spikes/5-treehouse-process-detection.md

items.title: #6 artifact byte-identity across slots at different paths
items.detail: Independent debug slots cost 12.8%-28% of slot 1 after dedup, 1.8% release. Remapping or CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 brings it under 3%. Clone-seeded plus one edit: 8.8%-10.3%. Slot-specific remap makes a copied target dirty. Mount namespaces (#17) not needed for dedup on these crates. Two small crates, one run per cell. docs/spikes/6-artifact-byte-identity.md

items.title: #18 decision: warm and incremental builds 2.5x-3.5x over NFS loopback
items.detail: Decided: reframe criterion 2 for macOS warm builds (option 1 of the follow-up plan). 1.5x stays for Linux and for macOS clean builds and git status; macOS warm/incremental builds get a provisional absolute budget (edit-and-rebuild adds under 1 s), amended in docs/design.md. v1 adopts AppleDouble translation, a readdir cache with a cookie verifier and the SETATTR guard fix. Option 3 (FUSE-T, macFUSE) is deferred to #37, after the full solution is built.

items.detail: Critic verdict: NOT mergeable. F1 deadlock: ensure_file holds the node write lock then takes the meta read lock while commit holds meta write then node read (repro hangs; builder's stress/kill9 never hit it). F2 promote_base removes base then forks: a failed fork loses base. F3 one corrupt block wedges the whole snapshot (fsync, readdir, fork, merkle_root all return Corrupt; other files' acked data lost at reopen) and a partial overwrite inside a corrupt chunk succeeds. Also: virtual inos reused across restart (wrong bytes), snapshot names accept .git/newline/ESC and case/NFC duplicates unlike the CLI, readdir flushes unrelated dirty data (48 MiB, 179 ms), alias table unbounded (469 MB after 500k creates), zero-id hole refs look dangling to GC. Held up: durability ordering, fsx 20k ops vs model, 60 s of overlapping writers (0 torn), hook failure recovery, EIO on corrupt reads. Bench (load 11-15): seq read 1351 MiB/s (13.6x slower than APFS page cache), 4K read 21.6k/s, seq write+fsync 390 MiB/s, lookups faster than std::fs. Builder fixing and re-merging fixed store and meta.

items.title: CI wall-clock: shard cargo test across parallel runner jobs
items.owner: DECISION for Zee: pre-registered wall-clock criterion missed (queue noise); job-time criteria met
items.status_note: 2026-10-09: PR175 (nextest, 2 ubuntu shards + 1 macOS job, aggregate check) MERGED by Zee at 07:31Z, overriding the pre-registered close rule (gain was inside noise: macOS test step 985 s vs 1023 s, wall 1109 s vs 1194 s, no same-window control). Decision made; stays on main.
log_20261008: 2026-10-08 measurement (main run 37844866363, cache hit): compile is already cached - ubuntu ~40s, macOS ~57s of the test step; the step is 783s ubuntu / 844s macOS, so ~740s is test EXECUTION: 170 test binaries run serially, top10 = 445s (real_project_acceptance 122s, admission 63s, locks 61s, requirements19 55s, conformance 35s ...); 105 binaries under 1s. Caching the build dir will not help. Options: shard across parallel jobs (cargo-nextest --partition count:N/M) for wall-clock win without adding in-runner contention that worsens the timing-sensitive tests (#79/#164 flakes); nextest in one runner mostly helps CPU headroom only. macOS minutes cost 10x if the repo is private (check).

Approved: run the tests in parallel. Plan: cargo-nextest with --partition across N parallel jobs per OS (hash partitioning), measured on a throwaway branch before the PR; keep fmt/clippy in their own parallel job; keep tests that need exclusive resources (mounts, fixed ports, timing-sensitive shutdown tests, --test-threads=1 jobs) in serial groups. Baseline to beat: ubuntu 783s / macOS 844s test step (compile already cached ~40-57s). Success = wall-clock per OS and no new flakes over >=5 consecutive green runs.

2026-10-08: PR175 open (ci/parallel-tests): lint / bench / test (os x 3 hash shards via cargo nextest, doctests on shard 1) / aggregate check (!cancelled()); .config/nextest.toml: no retries, cowfs-ctl + real_project_acceptance + gc collect race run alone (threads-required num-cpus), resource_bounds serialized; test shards share rust-cache key 'check' so PRs restore main's cache. Advisor-audited design. To prove: tests-run sum per OS equals the old single job, slowest-shard wall clock vs 783s/844s, 5 consecutive green runs. After merge: every open PR/agent must rebase, job names change from check (<os>) to test (<os>, <shard>) + check; critic prompts must grep test names in test shard logs (nextest 'PASS [ Ns ] crate::binary test').

2026-10-08 late: PR175 first run (1abb924, cold cache: shared-key was test-<os> so no hit) = wall 915s vs main 963s; per-job much faster (ubuntu shards 184-325s vs 783s step; macOS shards 277-428s vs 844s) but two of three macOS shards waited 291s and 480s for a free macOS runner, so end-to-end was not faster. Merge hazard: job names change (check (os) -> test (os, n, of) + check).

items.title: #204 macOS NFS mount: open() of a fifo gives EACCES (pjdfstest open/17.t #2, expected ENXIO)
items.status_note: 2026-10-09: investigated, macOS NFS CLIENT limitation, not a cowfs server bug. nfs_vnop_open returns EACCES for any vnode that is not reg/dir/lnk (apple-oss NFS kext/nfs_vnops.c); fifo gets regular NFS vnode ops (FIFO undefined in the NFS build, inferred from pathconf equal to a regular file). Open sends zero RPCs; fails for modes 000-777, O_EVTONLY/O_SYMLINK/O_EXEC, sandbox off, without the provenance xattr. No mount option helps.
